content:
Let \(G_n\) have vertices \(1,\dots,n\), with edges joining pairs whose sum is a square. We need the least \(n\) for which \(G_n\) has a Hamiltonian path.

For \(n=14\), vertices \(8,9,10\) each have degree \(1\): their only possible neighbors are \(1,7,6\), respectively. A Hamiltonian path has only two endpoints, so it cannot contain three degree-\(1\) vertices. Thus no \(n\le 14\) works (smaller \(n\) give similar degree-\(1\) obstructions or isolated vertices).

For \(n=15\), the sequence
\[
8,1,15,10,6,3,13,12,4,5,11,14,2,7,9
\]
has adjacent sums
\[
9,16,25,16,9,16,25,16,9,16,25,16,9,16,
\]
all perfect squares.

Therefore, the smallest value is \(\boxed{15}\).
